items.headline: BoJ raises policy rate to around 1.25%, effective 24 September
items.summary: The 18 September MPM lifted the uncollateralized overnight call target to around 1.25% (from ~1.0%) by a 7–2 vote, citing approaching 2% underlying CPI, Middle East energy risks, and spillover into consumer prices; complementary deposit facility rate also set at 1.25% from 24 September.

items.headline: BoC September deliberations: energy shock keeps near-term CPI elevated, limited pass-through so far
items.summary: Summary of deliberations (16 September) ahead of the 2 September hold at 2.25% said gasoline-driven headline CPI near 3% could persist, upside inflation risks have risen with prolonged Middle East conflict, and governors would consider hikes if energy costs broaden into core prices.

items.headline: RBA Governor Bullock: housing correction larger than expected but stability risks contained
items.summary: In 18 September parliamentary testimony, Bullock said housing has softened more than expected, prices remain ~50% above early-2020 levels, negative-equity shares are limited, and monetary policy targets inflation/activity rather than house prices.

items.headline: RBA Assistant Governor Hunter: rapid housing downturn within historical norms; oil shocks a key risk
items.summary: Podcast published 22 September (recorded 7 September) reiterated house prices are not targeted, described the current downturn as rapid but not unprecedented, and flagged ongoing oil/geopolitical shocks as complicating the inflation outlook ahead of the next Board meeting.

items.headline: BoE holds Bank Rate at 3.75% in 6–3 vote; energy path lifts CPI forecast
items.summary: September MPC minutes (16 September decision) kept Bank Rate at 3.75% with three dissenters favoring 4.00%; staff expect CPI to rise toward ~3.75% in Q4 2026 and slightly above 4% in early 2027 on energy, while unanimously approving a gilt QT plan averaging £46bn/year to zero by 2034.

items.headline: ECB September hike: energy keeps headline inflation above target into H1 2027
items.summary: At the 10 September meeting the Governing Council raised key rates 25bp, citing August euro-area headline CPI at 3.3% with energy inflation at 14.3%; staff project headline inflation returning near 2% toward end-2027.

items.headline: RBNZ lifts OCR 25bp to 2.75% on energy-driven inflation
items.summary: The 2 September MPS increased OCR to 2.75% by consensus, noting June-quarter CPI at 4.1% (fuel-driven), expectation inflation stays above 3% through 2026, and openness to further hikes if needed to reach the 2% midpoint by late 2027.

items.headline: Fed September FOMC: unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%; SEP median one further 2026 increase
items.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
items.summary: The 16 September statement and SEP showed a unanimous quarter-point increase, removal of accommodation language, median 2026 year-end funds rate at 4.1%, and Chair Warsh emphasizing inflation remains too high without offering explicit forward guidance.

method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Canada, Australia and ECB FX are required preflight inputs. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks; FST3/€STR stays observe_only until a public settlement feed is reliable. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.

items.headline: Oil rebounds in early 22 September trade on U.S.–Iran headlines and supply risks
items.summary: CNBC reported Brent November futures up about 1.2% near $101.54/bbl and WTI October up about 0.8% near $96.55/bbl early Tuesday, after Monday’s selloff, as traders weighed UN-week diplomacy against Middle East supply concerns.

items.headline: Reuters: Brent climbs back above $100 after four-session losing streak
items.summary: Reuters wire reports cited on 22 September showed Brent November up roughly 1–1.7% toward $102/bbl and WTI October higher toward the mid-$90s to high-$90s, with investors awaiting potential U.S.–Iran engagement at the UN General Assembly.

items.headline: Oil rises as Saudi export disruptions keep Hormuz supply in focus
items.summary: Anadolu Agency reported Brent November near $101.70/bbl (+1.4%) and WTI November near $93.35/bbl (+1%+) on 22 September, citing continued concern about Saudi export disruptions and broader Middle East supply risks.

items.headline: Monday oil hit multi-day lows on diplomacy hopes before Tuesday rebound
items.summary: Reuters reported Brent November fell to about $99.51/bbl (-4.2%) on Monday 21 September and WTI October fell about 5.3% to $95/bbl, the weakest closes in roughly 12 days, as markets priced possible UN diplomacy and partial Saudi flow recovery.

items.headline: Chicago Fed national activity index slips to -0.04 in August
items.summary: The Chicago Fed CFNAI for August 2026 was -0.04 versus a revised +0.08 in July; the three-month average CFNAI-MA3 rose to +0.01, consistent with growth around trend rather than recessionary readings.

items.headline: U.S. industrial production flat in August; manufacturing output falls 0.3%
items.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
items.summary: The Fed’s G.17 release showed total IP unchanged in August after +0.2% in July, manufacturing down 0.3%, utilities up 1.8%, and capacity utilization steady at 76.3%.

items.headline: U.S. import prices rise 0.7% in August; export prices up 0.6%
items.summary: BLS reported August import prices +0.7% m/m (+7.0% y/y) with fuel -0.1% but nonfuel +0.8%; export prices +0.6% m/m (+8.6% y/y), highlighting persistent external price pressure despite recent fuel volatility.

items.headline: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey still expanding but price indexes firm
items.source_name: National Association of Manufacturers (Philadelphia Fed survey)
items.summary: The September Philadelphia Fed general activity index fell to 37.8 from 47.4; prices paid rose to 48.6 and prices received to 31.3, indicating continued expansion with input-cost pressure.
